A car wash is a short machine that does the same thing every time, in the same order, to every car: soap, brushes, rinse, wax, dry. A machine like that can be written as a list of rungs, one per step, each latching the next; you have done that on the bottle line. It can also be written as a table: one row a step, each row saying which outputs are on and what the step waits for, and one instruction that walks down the table. That is what a sequencer is, and this chapter is about the two Logix instructions that make one, SQO (Sequencer Output) and SQI (Sequencer Input). the car wash is in Logix Connect as a classic scene, under File → New Project, opening with its guided track and its own machine faults. It takes its look from the PLCLogix 5000 car wash: a glass tunnel on an orange steel frame, a solar roof, dark portals, a pay station with a boom and yellow bollards.

The machine

Drivers arrive by themselves (Cars per minute) and stop at the pay terminal. When it says PAY HERE they pay, BASIC or DELUXE (Drivers who buy DELUXE; DELUXE adds wax), and wait for the boom. With the boom up they pull forward while the sign over the entry says DRIVE ON, until the front wheel stands on the first treadle, TS1, at the mouth of the conveyor, and put the car in neutral. From then on the conveyor moves the car: a roller pops up behind the left front wheel and pushes. It is a stop-and-go wash: the conveyor carries the car to a station, the program stops it with the wheel on that station’s treadle, the station works, the conveyor carries it on. The last station is the dryer, built into the exit portal: blowers each side and three producers on the portal pointing down at the car. Then the sign says DRIVE OUT and the driver pulls off the conveyor into the lot. About half the drivers (Drivers who stop at the free vacuums) take a free vacuum bay, vacuum the car for half a minute or so and back out; everybody leaves by the one-way EXIT ONLY lane to MAIN ST. Each car leaves the log a verdict: clean and dry, or what it missed (no soap, brushed dry, still soapy, still wet, no wax on a DELUXE).

Every sensor is where the car stands, and you can see it. At each of the seven stations a photo-eye pair crosses the bay at bumper height, the emitter on the south side and the reflector on the north, and a treadle sits in the trough where the front wheel stops. The name tags along the wall, PE1 ENTRY to PE7 EXIT, light an LED for each. Behind the tunnel, the equipment room: a water tank and a soap tank, each with a LO and a HI level switch, a pump to the arches and a fill valve; they show their level in percent and on the analog inputs.

Day and night

Like the parking gate, the wash runs through the day and the night on the run’s own clock (Day length, 24 minutes by default; Start hour). At night a car wash is its own advertisement: the tunnel glows through its glass, the arches light up in their colours (soap pink, brushes blue, rinse cyan, wax amber), the signs and the pylon shine, the cars come in with their headlights on.

Try it: click the machine

Click the pay terminal and the waiting driver pays at once. Click a tank (in the plan, in the side view’s inset, or in 3D) and it drains to 12 %. Click the road on the left and another car pulls in. Then drain the soap tank while a car is on its way to SOAP, and watch it wait.

The step table

Write the wash down the way the operator would describe it, a step at a time, and every step has three things: what is on, what it waits for, how long. Number the steps from 1, keep step 0 as HOME (nothing on), and you have a table of fourteen rows:

The output word, Wash_Out, has one bit for each thing a step can turn on: 0 the DRIVE ON sign, 1 the conveyor, 2 soap, 3 brushes, 4 rinse, 5 wax, 6 dryer, 7 DRIVE OUT, and bit 8, Dwell, which is not an output at all: it tells the dwell timer to run. The input word, Wash_In, has a bit for everything a step can wait for: the seven treadles in bits 0 to 6, the payment in bit 7, the dwell timer done in bit 8. Read the SOAP row: out 2#1_0000_0100 is Dwell and Soap; in 2#1_0000_0010 is TS2 and the timer done: soap the car standing on TS2 until the timer runs out. The underscores are only for your eyes, like the commas in 1,000.

The program’s index

Exercise 1: Init and the table

Init runs on the first scan. Its first rung clears what a power cut leaves half done and sends the sequencer HOME: RES on a CONTROL clears its position and its status bits, as it does on a timer. Then one rung per row of the table: three MOVs each. In a plant you would type the values into the tag editor once and never see them in the ladder; here they are written on the first scan so you can read the table where the logic is.

…and so on down to EXIT; the full table is above.

Watch for: element 0

SQO never writes element 0 while it walks: it steps POS from 1 to LEN and wraps back to 1. Element 0 is the HOME row, the one Init and RESET leave you in. A table with a real step in element 0 would run it once, after a reset, and never again.

Exercise 2: run, stop and reset

Exercise 3: SQI looks, SQO steps

This is the routine the chapter is about. The first rung gathers the inputs into Wash_In, one bit each, because SQI compares one word. The second asks SQI whether that word, through the mask, equals the step’s row of In_Table; SQI reads the step from the same CONTROL the SQO uses and never moves it. The mask, 16#01FF, is nine ones: compare all nine bits. If they match, Step_Done. Then SQO: on the change of its rung from false to true it steps the position on and copies the new row of Out_Table into Wash_Out, through its own mask. Last, the dwell: the step’s time from Dwell[Wash_Ctl.POS] into the timer’s preset, and the timer runs while the step’s Dwell bit is on.

Exercise 4: pay, the boom, onto the conveyor

PAY HERE lights only when the wash can take the next car: running, at LOAD, nobody paid yet. The payment latches Car_Paid, which is bit 7 of Wash_In: LOAD waits for a paid car with its wheel on TS1. Once the sequencer has moved on, Car_Paid is cleared so the next car has to pay for itself. The boom goes up for the paid car and down once its front wheel is on TS1, by which time its back bumper is well past the arm.

Exercise 5: the stations, and what a table cannot know

Each output takes its bit of Wash_Out, and each adds what a table cannot hold. Running and no fault on all of them. A car in front of the arch: the eye. Soap in the tank before the soap pump runs: a pump run dry is a pump replaced. Water before the brushes turn: brushes on a dry car leave swirl marks in the paint. The brush motor’s overload. DELUXE for the wax. The water pump runs for whatever needs water.

Exercise 6: the tanks, between their switches

Two switches make a band: open the fill at LO, keep it open (the seal-in) until HI. With one switch the valve would chatter on and off at the switch point.

Exercise 7: the watchdog, the cross-check, the lamps

Machine faults on the car wash

Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists the faults that belong to the parts on this floor. Each has a fault card: the symptom, what to watch in the I/O to confirm it, the repair, and what a program should do about it. Repair on an active fault removes its cause the way a technician would; whether the machine runs again is up to the program. The reference catches all five: the conveyor watchdog the dead treadle and the broken chain, the overload by its own contact, the dead eye by the cross-check, the leak by the fill watchdog.

Guided: the car wash

The scene opens with its guided track: Init (the table), Run, Sequence (watch POS go from HOME to LOAD and wait), Entry (a car pays and comes on; the sequencer moves although nothing moves yet), Stations (now the car goes through), Supply (drain the soap tank and watch it fill), Alarms and Ready. The sequencer is a lesson before the stations on purpose: you see the table being walked before anything is wired to it.

Try it: change the recipe without touching the logic

Give the brushes nine seconds: MOV(9000,Dwell[5]) in its row of Init. Then let the dryer keep blowing while the car is carried out: change TO EXIT’s output row from 2#0_0000_0010 to 2#0_0100_0010, conveyor and dryer. Run it: no output rung changed, the dryer rung still only blows while PE6 sees the car. On a program written as a latch per step, count the rungs you would have touched.

A tunnel that never stops

This is the same tunnel with its conveyor running all the time, slower, so three or four cars ride through at once. The step sequencer of the first car wash cannot run it: a sequencer has one step, and here every car is at a different station. So the program tracks the cars. The conveyor's drive sprocket has a prox, Conv_Pulse: a pulse every 8 units the chain moves. On every pulse a BSL (bit shift left) shifts the entry eye's state into Track: bit 0 is what the eye sees now, bit 1 what it saw one pulse ago — 8 units further in — and so on to bit 63. A car's body is a run of 1s walking up the array, and each station looks at the one slot under its arch: soap 8, brushes 18, rinse 28, wax 38, dryer 52. Pulses, not time: stop the conveyor and the cars stand still and so does the tracking. The tags are made; the conveyor runs at 10 (the first car wash runs at 24).

START, STOP and RESET

START seals Running in; STOP is normally closed, so XIC of its input lets the rung through; a fault drops Running. RESET clears the fault once the brush overload is reset.

Run it
  • Press START: Running

The gap, the payment, onto the conveyor

The next car may come on only when there is room: the eye clear, and slots 0-5 behind it empty. MEQ(Track[0],16#3F,0) is a masked equal: it compares only the bits set in the mask, slots 0-5, with 0. With the gap, PAY HERE; the payment latches Car_Paid (and Deluxe_Car for DELUXE); the boom and DRIVE ON let the paid car drive on; its front wheel on TS1 uses the payment up and counts one more in the tunnel. Nothing carries it yet: the conveyor is the next lesson.

Run it
  • A car pays (Car_Paid)
  • …drives on: its wheel on TS1, In_Tunnel 1

The shift registers

The conveyor runs with the wash. On every Conv_Pulse both BSLs shift: Track takes the eye (PE1_Entry), Wax_Trk takes the eye AND DELUXE (Wax_Bit). The length is 64 bits, so each starts at element [0] and runs on into [1]. Watch Track[0] in Quick Watch as a car passes the eye: a run of 1s appears at the bottom and climbs by one bit a pulse.

Run it
  • START: the conveyor runs
  • …and a car is a run of bits in Track

Each station reads its slot

Each station is on while its slot holds a car — XIC of one bit — plus what the bit cannot know: running and no fault, soap in the tank, water and a healthy motor for the brushes. Slot 38 is bit 6 of the second element, so the wax reads Wax_Trk[1].6. DRIVE OUT stays lit: the cars leave as they come off the end, counted at the exit eye.

Run it
  • The soap arch runs for the first car
  • Two cars in the tunnel at once
  • …and a car comes out washed (Car_Count)

Filling the tanks

The same as the first car wash: each tank fills from its low switch to its high switch, the soap fill has a watchdog. Click the soap tank in the equipment room to drain it.

Run it
  • The soap tank fills (Soap_Fill)
  • …to its high switch

The pulse watchdog

A tracking program trusts its pulses, so it watches them. Pulse_Edge is on for one scan at every pulse and resets the watchdog timer; the conveyor on for 3 s without a pulse means the chain has broken (or the prox is dead) and nothing in Track is where it says any more: a fault, everything stops. Break the chain below.

Run it
  • The chain breaks: Wash_Fault latches
  • …RESET clears it after the repair

Running, and what to try

Press STOP with three cars inside, wait, press START: every station picks up where it was, because the tracking only moves with the chain. Make the conveyor faster or slower in the wash's properties: the slots stay right (they are distances, not times), only the time each car spends under an arch changes — too fast and the cars come out still wet. Watch a BASIC car go under the wax arch dark. Then compare with the first car wash: one car at a time, a sequencer, a dwell at every station. Same tunnel, same tags, two ways to run it.

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Wash_Fault is unlatched, Car_Paid is unlatched, Supply_Alarm is unlatched, Wash_Ctl is reset and Wash_Out is written.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung unlatches Wash_Fault (Latched by the conveyor watchdog or the brush overload; RESET clears it), unlatches Car_Paid (A car has paid at the terminal and may come on (only while the sequencer is at LOAD)), unlatches Supply_Alarm (The soap tank did not fill in time (a leak, an empty drum)), resets Wash_Ctl (The sequencer: .POS is the step (0 HOME, 1 LOAD ... 13 EXIT), .LEN 13; SQO moves it, SQI reads it) and clears Wash_Out (The step's outputs, one bit each: 0 Enter, 1 Conveyor, 2 Soap, 3 Brushes, 4 Rinse, 5 Wax, 6 Dryer, 7 Exit, 8 Dwell) to 0.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 5 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Running on, and Running’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 1
rungs.comment: STEP DONE when the inputs match the step's row of In_Table (all nine bits, the mask 16#01FF), or at HOME, or for a BASIC car at WAX
rungs.words: When either (the inputs in Wash_In (The inputs a step waits for, gathered into one word: bits 0-6 the treadles TS1-TS7, 7 Car_Paid, 8 the dwell timer done) match the step’s row of In_Table[0] (The input word every step waits for)), (Wash_Ctl.POS (the position of Wash_Ctl: The sequencer: .POS is the step (0 HOME, 1 LOAD ... 13 EXIT), .LEN 13; SQO moves it, SQI reads it) equals 0) or (Wash_Ctl.POS equals 9 and Deluxe_Car (The car being washed bought DELUXE: the wax arch runs for it) is off), the rung turns Step_Done (The inputs match the step's row (or HOME, or a BASIC car at WAX): step on) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. SQI(In_Table[0],16#01FF,Wash_In,Wash_Ctl,13,0) Sequencer Input asks: true when the inputs in Wash_In match the step’s row of In_Table[0]. It reads the position from the control and never moves it.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Wash_Ctl.POS,0) Equal asks: true when Wash_Ctl.POS equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 3
    1. EQU(Wash_Ctl.POS,9) Equal asks: true when Wash_Ctl.POS equals 9. Both values are compared every scan.
    2. XIO(Deluxe_Car) Examine If Open asks: true when Deluxe_Car is off.
  2. OTE(Step_Done) Output Energize does: turns Step_Done on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: A sequencer: the table holds the order.
pats.why: The steps and what each one turns on live in a table, not in rungs; the program moves the position and the table does the rest.
pats.think: a music box drum: the pins are the table, and turning the drum one notch plays the next row.
pats.watch: Change the order of the machine in the table, not in the rungs, and check the mask: a bit outside it is never written.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 2
rungs.comment: A car finished: counted as the EXIT step completes

rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Wash_Ctl.POS,13) Equal asks: true when Wash_Ctl.POS equals 13. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Step_Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Step_Done is on.
  3. ONS(Exit_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Exit_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. ADD(Car_Count,1,Car_Count) Add does: makes Car_Count = Car_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Sequence · Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE SEQUENCER. When Step_Done comes true SQO steps .POS on (after 13 it wraps to 1, LOAD) and copies that row of Out_Table into Wash_Out. rungs.words: When Running (The wash is running: START seals it in, STOP (normally closed) or a fault drops it) is on, Wash_Fault (Latched by the conveyor watchdog or the brush overload; RESET clears it) is off, Step_Done (The inputs match the step's row (or HOME, or a BASIC car at WAX): step on) is on and Wash_Ctl.EN (the enable bit of Wash_Ctl: The sequencer: .POS is the step (0 HOME, 1 LOAD ... 13 EXIT), .LEN 13; SQO moves it, SQI reads it) is off, the rung steps Wash_Ctl (The sequencer: .POS is the step (0 HOME, 1 LOAD ... 13 EXIT), .LEN 13; SQO moves it, SQI reads it) on one row and writes that row of Out_Table[0] (The output word of every step (element 0 = HOME)) to Wash_Out (The step's outputs, one bit each: 0 Enter, 1 Conveyor, 2 Soap, 3 Brushes, 4 Rinse, 5 Wax, 6 Dryer, 7 Exit, 8 Dwell).

pats.t: A sequencer: the table holds the order.

rungs.comment: …and the timer runs while the step's Dwell bit is on. TON(T_Step,?,?): the ? means the preset is the tag's own .PRE, the one the MOV wrote

    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB_Pressed is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Running) Examine If Closed asks: true when Running is on.

rungs.head: Track · Rung 2
rungs.comment: THE TRACKING. Every pulse from the sprocket (the conveyor moved 8 units) both registers shift one slot: the entry eye's state goes into slot 0 and everything else moves up one. A BSL shifts on the rung going true, so one pulse is one shift, however long the pulse is. No pulse, no shift: stopped, the tracking holds
rungs.words: When Conv_Pulse (Wash Conv_Pulse: Conveyor pulse: a prox on the drive sprocket, one pulse every 8 units the chain moves (on for the first 4, off for the next 4)) is on, the rung shifts Track[0] (The tunnel, one bit per slot of conveyor (8 units): bit n is what the entry eye saw n pulses ago. Track[0] holds slots 0-31, Track[1] slots 32-63) one place left, bringing in PE1_Entry (Wash PE1_Entry: Photo-eye 1 (ENTRY) across the bay at bumper height: 1 while a car blocks it) and shifts Wax_Trk[0] (The same slots, 1 only for a DELUXE car: the wax reads it) one place left, bringing in Wax_Bit (What goes into Wax_Trk on a pulse: the entry eye blocked AND the car is DELUXE).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Pulse) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Pulse is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. BSL(Track[0],Track_Ctl,PE1_Entry,64) Bit Shift Left does: shifts Track[0] one place left, bringing in PE1_Entry. One shift per false-to-true transition of the rung.
    Path 2
    1. BSL(Wax_Trk[0],Wax_Ctl,Wax_Bit,64) Bit Shift Left does: shifts Wax_Trk[0] one place left, bringing in Wax_Bit. One shift per false-to-true transition of the rung.

pats.t: A shift register.
pats.why: Every bit of the word is a position on the conveyor; one shift per index moves every part’s bit one position along, so a bit at a station says what is standing there.
pats.think: a row of pigeonholes riding along with the conveyor. Put a note in the first hole when a part arrives; every index moves every note one hole along.
pats.watch: The shift has to happen exactly once per index. Drive it from a one-shot or a transition, never from a level that stays true.

pred.q: Water_Low is on, Water_Fill is off and Water_High is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Water_Fill is on.

rungs.words: When either (Water_Low (Wash Water_Low: Water tank low level switch: 1 below 20 %) is on) or (Water_Fill (Wash Water_Fill: Water tank fill valve (city water)) is on) and Water_High (Wash Water_High: Water tank high level switch: 1 above 90 %) is off, the rung turns Water_Fill on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Water_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Water_Low is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Water_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when Water_Fill is on.
  2. XIO(Water_High) Examine If Open asks: true when Water_High is off.
  3. OTE(Water_Fill) Output Energize does: turns Water_Fill on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: Seal-in.
pats.why: The start condition turns Water_Fill on, and Water_Fill’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.

rungs.head: Supply · Rung 2
rungs.comment: A soap fill that has not reached the high switch in 40 s: a leak, or the bulk drum is empty

pred.q: Soap_Fill is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: T_SoapFill is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(Soap_Fill).

rungs.words: When Soap_Fill (Wash Soap_Fill: Soap tank fill valve (from the bulk drum)) is on, the rung runs the timer T_SoapFill (Soap fill watchdog: 40 s without reaching the high switch is a supply alarm) toward 40000 ms (40 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Soap_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when Soap_Fill is on.
  2. TON(T_SoapFill,40000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_SoapFill toward 40000 ms (40 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_SoapFill counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Supply · Rung 3
rungs.words: When T_SoapFill.DN (the done bit of T_SoapFill: Soap fill watchdog: 40 s without reaching the high switch is a supply alarm) is on, the rung latches Supply_Alarm (The soap tank did not fill in time (a leak, an empty drum)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_SoapFill.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_SoapFill.DN is on.
  2. OTL(Supply_Alarm) Output Latch does: latches Supply_Alarm on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.t: A latch.
pats.why: Supply_Alarm stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Supply · Rung 4
rungs.comment: RESET clears it once the fill has stopped

pred.q: Reset_PB_Pressed is on and Soap_Fill is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Supply_Alarm is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Reset_PB_Pressed (Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on and Soap_Fill (Wash Soap_Fill: Soap tank fill valve (from the bulk drum)) is off, the rung unlatches Supply_Alarm (The soap tank did not fill in time (a leak, an empty drum)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. XIO(Soap_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when Soap_Fill is off.
  3. OTU(Supply_Alarm) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Supply_Alarm. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Supply_Alarm when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 2

pred.q: T_F1.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Fl_Bit is on.

rungs.words: When T_F1.DN (the done bit of T_F1: Flasher, half a second on) is on, the rung turns Fl_Bit (The flasher bit) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_F1.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_F1.DN is on.
  2. OTE(Fl_Bit) Output Energize does: turns Fl_Bit on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 3
rungs.comment: THE CONVEYOR WATCHDOG. Pulse_Edge is on for one scan at every pulse…
rungs.words: When Conv_Pulse (Wash Conv_Pulse: Conveyor pulse: a prox on the drive sprocket, one pulse every 8 units the chain moves (on for the first 4, off for the next 4)) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Pulse_Edge (On for one scan at every conveyor pulse) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conv_Pulse) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conv_Pulse is on.
  2. ONS(Pulse_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Pulse_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. OTE(Pulse_Edge) Output Energize does: turns Pulse_Edge on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 4
rungs.comment: …and resets the timer (its rung goes false for that scan). The conveyor on for 3 s with no pulse: the chain has broken or the prox is dead, and the tracking is wrong from here on

pred.q: Conveyor is on and Pulse_Edge is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: T_Pulse is reset to 0. It stops at XIO(Pulse_Edge).

rungs.words: When Conveyor (Wash Conveyor: Tunnel conveyor motor: the roller pushes the front wheel) is on and Pulse_Edge (On for one scan at every conveyor pulse) is off, the rung runs the timer T_Pulse (Conveyor watchdog: running 3 s with no pulse is a broken chain or a dead prox) toward 3000 ms (3 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Conveyor) Examine If Closed asks: true when Conveyor is on.
  2. XIO(Pulse_Edge) Examine If Open asks: true when Pulse_Edge is off.
  3. TON(T_Pulse,3000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Pulse toward 3000 ms (3 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Pulse counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

  2. OTL(Wash_Fault) Output Latch does: latches Wash_Fault on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Wash_Fault stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Alarms · Rung 7
rungs.comment: FAULT steady for a stop, flashing for the supply alarm
rungs.words: When either (Wash_Fault (Latched by the conveyor watchdog or the brush overload; RESET clears it) is on) or (Supply_Alarm (The soap tank did not fill in time (a leak, an empty drum)) is on and Fl_Bit (The flasher bit) is on), the rung turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:

    1. XIC(Wash_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when Wash_Fault is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Supply_Alarm) Examine If Closed asks: true when Supply_Alarm is on.
    2. XIC(Fl_Bit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fl_Bit is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
